claim: The Legislature convenes its first regular session on the first Wednesday of December after the general election
quote: convene on the first Wednesday of December following the general election in what shall be designated the first regular session of the Legislature

claim: The second regular session convenes the first Wednesday after the first Tuesday of January of the even-numbered year and is limited in scope
quote: shall further convene on the first Wednesday after the first Tuesday of January in the subsequent even-numbered year in what shall be designated the second regular session of the Legislature

claim: The second session is limited to budget, emergency, governor-called, carried-over study and initiated legislation
quote: the business of the second regular session of the Legislature shall be limited to budgetary matters

claim: The Legislature may also convene on call of the presiding officers with majority-party consent
quote: The Legislature may convene at such other times on the call of the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House

claim: The first regular session must adjourn by the third Wednesday in June; the second by the third Wednesday in April; limited extensions allowed
quote: The first regular session of the Legislature, after its convening, may not adjourn later than the 3rd Wednesday in June and the 2nd regular session of the Legislature may not adjourn later than the 3rd Wednesday in April

claim: The governor has 10 days, Sundays excepted, to act; a bill held when adjournment prevents return becomes law unless returned within 3 days after the next meeting of the same Legislature
quote: unless returned within 3 days after the next meeting of the same Legislature which enacted the bill or resolution

claim: Governor 10-day rule
quote: If the bill or resolution shall not be returned by the Governor within 10 days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to the Governor

claim: Non-emergency acts take effect 90 days after the session recesses
quote: shall take effect until 90 days after the recess of the session of the Legislature in which it was passed

claim: An emergency act may not infringe municipal home rule
quote: an infringement of the right of home rule for municipalities

claim: The state primary is the second Tuesday of June of each general election year
quote: The primary election shall be held on the 2nd Tuesday of June of each general election year

claim: An unenrolled voter may vote in one party primary without enrolling
quote: A registered voter not enrolled in a political party may participate

claim: An unenrolled voter may vote in only one party primary
quote: An unenrolled voter may vote in only one party's primary election

claim: Ranked-choice voting applies only to primaries for U.S. Senate, U.S. House, governor and the Legislature, federal general elections, and presidential elections
quote: Primary elections for the offices of United States Senator, United States Representative to Congress, Governor, State Senator and State Representative

claim: Other primaries, including county office, are decided by plurality
quote: In a primary election, the person who receives a plurality of the votes cast for nomination to any office

claim: General and other elections not using ranked-choice voting are decided by plurality
quote: In any other election except for those determined by ranked-choice voting, the person who receives a plurality of the votes cast for election to any office

claim: County commissioners are elected in November of even-numbered years
quote: County commissioners shall be elected on the Tuesday following the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year

claim: The default board is a chair and two others, each elected from a commissioner district by its voters
quote: There shall be a board of commissioners for each county consisting of a chairman and 2 other persons

claim: Commissioners must live in and are elected by their district
quote: Members of each board of commissioners must be residents of the commissioner district which they represent and shall be elected by the voters of that district

claim: The commissioners pick their own chair each year
quote: The commissioners shall select their chairman annually

claim: York County has five commissioners
quote: there shall be a Board of Commissioners for York County consisting of a chair and 4 other citizens

claim: Commissioner terms are four years
quote: The term of office for a county commissioner is 4 years

claim: A vacancy in a primary-nominated commissioner seat is filled by appointee of the same party, showing county races are partisan
quote: the commissioner appointed by the Governor must be enrolled in the same political party as the commissioner whose term is vacant

claim: Each county elects a treasurer for four years, unless voters switched to an appointed treasurer
quote: the voters of each county shall elect a county treasurer

claim: A county may replace its elected treasurer with an appointed one, with voter approval
quote: the county commissioners may decide to abolish the position of elected county treasurer and replace it with an appointed county treasurer

claim: District attorneys are elected every four years by prosecutorial district, not by county
quote: The district attorneys shall be elected on the Tuesday following the first Monday of November in every 4th year, by the voters of the respective prosecutorial districts

claim: Sheriffs are elected by county by plurality for four years
quote: Sheriffs shall be elected by the people of their respective counties, by a plurality of the votes given in

claim: Judges and registers of probate are elected by county by plurality for four years
quote: Judges and registers of probate shall be elected by the people of their respective counties, by a plurality of the votes given in

claim: County office candidates must live and vote in the division they seek
quote: A candidate for the office of presidential elector or any county office must be a resident of and a voter in the electoral division

claim: A party-enrolled person who wants to run by petition must first withdraw enrollment by a deadline
quote: If enrolled, the person must also withdraw enrollment in a party

claim: A petition candidate may list a political designation of up to three words, not a qualified party name
quote: This designation may not exceed 3 words in length

claim: Counties may adopt charters setting their own structure
quote: The purpose of this chapter is to provide a method for each county, by vote of its voters, to determine the structure of county government in that county

claim: A county charter may provide for election of a county legislative body and how officers are selected
quote: The election of a county legislative body and the method of selecting officers, officials and employees

claim: A charter can displace the general laws on commissioners, treasurers and registers of deeds
quote: if the new charter abolishes any of these offices or positions

claim: Municipality includes cities, towns and plantations
quote: "Municipality" includes cities, towns and plantations

claim: Municipalities may amend their charters on local and municipal matters not prohibited by constitution or general law
quote: The inhabitants of any municipality shall have the power to alter and amend their charters on all matters, not prohibited by Constitution or general law, which are local and municipal in character

claim: Chapter 111 implements constitutional home rule
quote: The purpose of this chapter is to implement the home rule powers granted to municipalities by the Constitution of Maine

claim: Voters can force a charter commission by petition
quote: the municipal officers, by order, shall provide for the establishment of a charter commission

claim: Unless a charter or Title 30-A says otherwise, Title 21-A governs municipal voting
quote: Except as otherwise provided by this Title or by charter, the method of voting and the conduct of a municipal election are governed by Title

claim: Each town holds an annual meeting that elects a moderator, select board and school committee by ballot
quote: Each town shall hold an annual meeting at which the following town officials shall be elected by ballot

claim: A town may designate other officials to be elected by ballot
quote: may designate other town officials to be elected by ballot

claim: Town officials: plurality in towns over 4,000; majority in towns of 4,000 or fewer, unless the charter differs
quote: In a town with a population greater than 4,000, according to the last Federal Decennial Census, election shall be by plurality

claim: Small towns default to majority
quote: in a town with a population of 4,000 or under, election shall be by majority

claim: A town decides whether its select board has 3, 5 or 7 members and their terms
quote: whether 3, 5 or 7 will be elected to each board and their terms of office

claim: Under secret ballot rules, election is by plurality, with a runoff only to break a tie
quote: Election must be by plurality vote.  In the case of a tie vote, the municipal clerk shall automatically initiate a recount

claim: Nomination of town officials by political caucus applies only where a town separately accepts it
quote: The provisions of this section relating to the nomination of town officials by political caucus apply only when a town separately accepts those provisions

claim: City candidates nominated by petition may use a political designation only if the city charter permits
quote: A person seeking nomination under this section may use a political designation only if permitted by the city charter

claim: City elections are by plurality unless the charter says otherwise
quote: In a city election, unless otherwise provided by municipal charter, the person who receives a plurality of the votes cast for election to any office is elected to that office

claim: An unincorporated township of 200 or more may organize as a plantation, electing assessors, clerk and others
quote: to choose a moderator, clerk, 3 assessors, treasurer, collector of taxes, constable, school committee and other necessary plantation officers

claim: A plantation is one township
quote: Organized plantations may not be composed of more than one township

claim: A municipality not in a district elects a school committee at its annual meeting
quote: shall elect at its annual meeting a school committee of 3

claim: School administrative district directors are nominated as municipal officials
quote: school directors shall be considered municipal officials and shall be nominated in accordance with Title

claim: SAD boards have at least five directors including one from each member municipality
quote: It shall include at least one director from each municipality or subdistrict

claim: SAD director terms are three years with annual elections or four years with biennial elections
quote: In municipalities with annual elections, directors shall serve a 3-year term.  In municipalities with biennial elections, directors shall serve a 4-year term

claim: Portland's charter elects its mayor, city councilors and school board members by ranked choice voting
quote: For the positions of mayor, city councilor, and school board member, the city clerk shall implement a ranked choice voting protocol

claim: If no candidate has a majority of first choices, the city clerk runs an instant runoff
quote: If no candidate receives a majority of first choice votes, an instant runoff re-tabulation shall be promptly conducted by the city clerk
